title: 也 and 都 in Chinese: HSK 1 Grammar with Examples
description: Where to put 也 (yě, also) and 都 (dōu, all) in a Chinese sentence: word order, 也都, negatives, questions, the common mistake, and HSK 1 examples.
h1: 也 and 都: Word Order with "Also" and "All"
lede: 也 (yě) means "also" or "too", and 都 (dōu) means "all" or "both". They follow the same word-order rule: after the subject, before the verb or adjective. They never go at the start or the end of the sentence.

paras: In English, "too" can go at the end of the sentence. In Chinese, 也 always comes after the subject and before the verb or adjective, and also before words like 很, 不 and 想. This is true even when the "also" is about the object: "I like reading, and I also like films" is 我喜欢看书，也喜欢看电影, with 也 before the second 喜欢.

examples.zh: 我喜欢看书，也喜欢看电影。
examples.py: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn shū, yě xǐhuan kàn diànyǐng.
examples.en: I like reading, and I like watching films too.

paras: Plural subject + 都 + verb or adjective.

都 looks back at the words in front of it and says that all of them are included: we, these books, Mum and I. With two people or things it means "both". It is very common after time words such as 天天 (every day).

examples.py: Wǒ hé māma dōu xǐhuan kàn shū.
examples.en: Mum and I both like reading.
These books are all really good.

examples.py: Wǒ tiāntiān dōu qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
examples.en: I get up at seven every day.

paras: Learners often put 也 or 都 where the English word goes. 也我是学生 and 我是学生也 are both wrong; say 我也是学生. In the same way, "all of us are going" is 我们都去, never 都我们去.
Because 都 only looks backwards, the things it covers must come before it. To say "I like both of these", move 这两个 to the front: 这两个我都喜欢. And when you use 也 and 都 together, 也 comes first: 也都.

examples.py: Zhè liǎng ge wǒ dōu xǐhuan.
Tāmen yě dōu shì Zhōngguó rén.

paras: For negatives, 也 and 都 come before 不 or 没有. 也不 and 也没有 mean "not either". 都不 means "none of them", but 不都 means "not all of them", so the order changes the meaning.
To ask a question, just add 吗 at the end. The word order stays the same.

examples.en: Not all of them are students.
Do you want to go too?
